name: Pork Vindaloo
subtitle: Vinegar-and-garlic pork, descended from Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos

ingredients.qty: 800g shoulder, in large cubes with some fat

ingredients.note: palm vinegar if you can find it

prepNotes: Vindaloo is not simply 'very hot'. The name is vinha d'alhos — wine and garlic — and the defining flavours are sour and garlicky, with Kashmiri chillies for colour rather than fire.
Grind the masala with vinegar, never water. The vinegar is both the flavour and the preservative that let this dish travel.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger and whole spices with the vinegar to a smooth, thick paste. Use no water.
Rub half the paste into the pork with salt and marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight refrigerated.
Fry the onion in oil until soft and golden, then add the remaining masala paste and cook until the oil separates.
Add the pork with its marinade and turn it over high heat until sealed and coated.
Add a cup of hot water, cover, and simmer 60 minutes until the pork is tender and the fat has rendered into the gravy.
Balance with jaggery and salt. Rest overnight if you can — vindaloo is markedly better on day two.

storage: Genuinely improves for 3-4 days refrigerated; the vinegar preserves it. Freezes 3 months.
